item.title: Introduction
item.description:
Introduction

NONMEM stands for "Nonlinear Mixed Effects Model." Written in Fortran 90/95, NONMEM fits general nonlinear regression-type models to data. The data are typically collected from clinical studies of pharmaceutic agents, involving the administration of a drug to individuals and the subsequent observation of drug levels (most often in the blood plasma). Proper modeling of these data involves accounting for both inter- and intra-subject effects (random effects), as well as measured concomitant effects (fixed effects). This mixed effect modeling approach, and the nonlinear nature of the biochemical and physiological process involved, is the bedrock of NONMEM. Such modeling is especially useful when there are only a few pharmacokinetic measurements from each individual sampled in the population, or when the data collection design varies considerably between these individuals. However, NONMEM is a general program which can be used to fit models to a wide variety of data.
